notes: WHY MALONE '97 READ DEF 95, TERM BY TERM, BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED. drep 1.000 (unanimous All-Defensive 1st team), DBPM +1.2 = the 0.816 percentile of 1997, 81 inches, BLK% 1.3 = the 0.573 percentile. rep_hf at 81 in is 1.0667 and the height_inv term is 0.875, so his composite PD is 0.453*1.0667 + 0.238*0.816 + 0.309*0.875 = 0.4832 + 0.1942 + 0.2704 = 0.9477 - and 0.7536 of that 0.9477, 80% of the sheet, is the two HEIGHT-RATED terms. Pvot(0.9477) = 0.875, _paid_in_rim was 0.000, so PD2 = 0.55 + 0.45*0.875*1.000 = 0.9438, card 93.5, smoothed against '96 (92.70) and '98 (92.46) to 93. d_score then reads him as a BIG (d_bigness 1.0000) and takes 0.40 x perdef 93 + 0.40 x rimprot 74 + 0.17 x drb 92, raw 96.2338 against a DEF_TOP of 104.25 - DEF 95, level with Hakeem '94 and above Mutombo '97.

THE SECOND PAYMENT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. Set the reinforcement line ID = ID + 0.25*(drep*hp) to 0.00 in a scratch run and the board reads: Karl Malone '97 rimprot 56 (was 74), Buck Williams '91 52 (63), Rodman '93 49 (57), Charles Oakley '94 31 (46), Roundfield '82 77 (92), McHale '88 77 (91) - and Mutombo '97 99 (98), Hakeem '94 99 (99), i.e. the two DPOYs are carried by their blocks and do not need the line at all. Malone's All-Defensive votes are therefore worth EIGHTEEN points of rim protection, taken by the big d_score branch at 0.40, beside the 0.40 it takes of a perdef the same votes bought. recal_114 named exactly this double payment and metered it as drep x block evidence, which is 0.000 below the 80th percentile of the season's block rate - so on the one card where the rim paid the most, its verdict was that the rim had paid nothing.

WHY THE BOUNDARY IS 80 INCHES AND WHY IT IS NOT FITTED. This file draws the wing/big line in exactly one place and draws it twice: recal_35's sweet band is FLAT at 1.0 from 75 to 80 inches, and recal_54's rep_hf is FLAT at its maximum 1.2 through 80. Both then fade - but over 8 inches and 6, so a 6'9" power forward still collects 87.5% and 89% of the pure-WING rate. The new channel is that same band test, nothing more: 0 inside, 1 outside. It was NOT chosen to hit the number - the number is hit by recal_114's existing exponent, 0.816**3 = 0.542, which is why VOTE_SUPPORT_POW is untouched.

THE TWO SOFTER RAMPS WERE MEASURED AND MISSED. A 2-inch ramp (share 0.5 at 6'9") leaves the subject at perdef 85, DEF 91; a 3-inch ramp at perdef 85, DEF 91. Both are outside 87 +-3. Reaching the band with a softer ramp requires VOTE_SUPPORT_POW 5, which costs Roundfield '82 4 DEF, McHale '88 5, Bobby Jones '82 2 and Ben Wallace '04 1 for the same subject reading - a strictly larger footprint for a strictly worse justification, since 5 is a refitting of recal_114's own constant. Rejected.

THE PRICE, STATED PLAINLY. At 80 inches Buck Williams '91 keeps perdef 93; at 81 Malone reads 76. That discontinuity is real and it is the cost of the ruling as it was given. The boundary cannot move down: Dennis Rodman '90 (def 94 +-1, 79 in) and Scottie Pippen '03 (def 76 +-1, 80 in) are anchored on the inside of it, and Buck Williams '91 88 and Rodman '93 89 are the two comparables the ruling's target of 87 is read off - a fade beginning at 78 or 79 takes all four down with the subject and destroys the evidence the target rests on.

THE CLASS THAT MOVED IS THE CLASS THE RULING NAMES. All 193 perdef movers are voted cards above 80 inches: 104 at 81, 50 at 82, 38 at 83, 1 at 84. The largest are Karl Malone '95-'01, Charles Oakley '91-'96 (All-Defensive 1st team on a BLK% of 0.4, the 18th percentile of his season), Maurice Lucas, A.C. Green, Luol Deng, Tayshaun Prince, Ben Simmons, Bam Adebayo and LeBron James '14/'15 - 6'9"-6'11" forwards with All-Defensive votes, no rim deterrence and a DBPM that does not carry them. Every one of them keeps the share of the premium his DBPM percentile cubed supports, so the ordering inside the class is unchanged.

NOBODY ROSE. Because the deduction lands on the 0.45 vote premium and never on PD, the within-season Pvot pool is bit-identical: of 10,000 cards, 193 perdef moved and all 193 moved DOWN, 150 DEF moved and all 150 moved down, and the perdef top 12 is name-for-name and position-for-position what it was. This is recal_114's own design decision, reused rather than re-argued.

THE JAZZ DIALS, since the subject is the card story behind them (recal_122 named his perdef 92 as the reason the Jazz '98 defence dialled 91 for a real 17th-ranked defence). Read through data/anchors.py's team_dials on the OVR-max legal five - Stockton, Hornacek, Russell, Malone, Ostertag - Jazz '97 defdial 91 -> 83 and Jazz '98 defdial 91 -> 81. The within-season model DEF rank is 2nd of 29 and 2nd of 28 both before and after: the all-time LEVEL falls by 8 and 10 points, the season ORDER does not move, and moving it is team_rating.py's, not this agent's.

THE ONE OFF MOVER IS NOT A PERDEF EFFECT AND IS NOT MINE. Tayshaun Prince '04 o_ovr 48 -> 51 is the only offensive change on the board; it comes from compute_ovr.py's own reading of a card whose defensive sheet moved, not from anything build_ratings.py did to an offensive attribute. Flagged for ratings-to-off-def, not chased here.

WHERE 89 SITS IN THE BAND, HONESTLY. The ruling asked for near 87 with a +-3 band; the round lands 89, the top half. Reaching 87 exactly costs one more knob - VOTE_SUPPORT_POW 3 -> 4 takes him to 87.5 - and that constant is recal_114's fitted answer to a different ruling of his. One defensible change was the instruction, and the anchors are all inside their bands at 89.
cost: ANCHOR ADDED: Karl Malone '97 def 87 +-3 (round 135). Nothing superseded.

135 anchors, 0 failing, mean |error| 0.69 - identical worst three to origin/main (Warriors '17 defdial -5, Thunder '26 defdial +4, Westbrook '15 ballsec +4). On the 134 anchors that existed before this round the mean |error| improved 0.69 -> 0.68.

recal_114's meter is now COMPLETE for the rim, but it is still a meter of the rim only. A vote is also paid a third time in drb for a rebounding forward (0.17 of the big d_score); nothing in this round touches that, and a future ruling on a glass-first All-Defensive big should start there and not by re-cutting this channel.

THE BOUNDARY IS LOAD-BEARING. Any later round that widens the wing band past 80 inches, or that softens rep_hf's flat top, moves this channel with it - the height test reads the same 80.0 the band does, deliberately, so the two cannot drift apart.
rimprot moved on ZERO cards; o_ovr moved on ONE (Tayshaun Prince '04, +3). d_ovr 150 cards, ovr 107 cards, max OVR move -4 (Bam Adebayo '26).
